question: What is the primary job this application does for the user — in one sentence from their perspective?
answer: I come to Sherpy to plan a software project, and it guides me through the planning process step by step. It allows me to easily see all of my active and past projects. It allows me to work through its workflow at my own pace. Frequently I need to come back several times to add more information before I can complete a step. It helps me to pull the thread on planning all of the projects I am working on.

question: Who is the primary user?
answer: d) Product manager coordinating across engineering teams

question: When a PM creates a project in Sherpy, who else interacts with it?
answer: b) PM + engineers review/comment on the plan output

question: Does the PM always run all 10 steps, or do they pick the steps relevant to their project?
answer: d) App recommends. Two entry paths: (1) starting from scratch — skip gap analysis, go straight to business requirements interview; (2) starting with initial requirements doc — run gap analysis, generate gap worksheet, fill gaps, then business requirements interview. Gap worksheet gaps must be resolved before proceeding.

question: On the project dashboard, what does the PM most need to see at a glance for each project?
answer: a) Name + current step + last-touched date. Additionally each project has an auto-generated project-code for reference — visible on the dashboard card.

question: When a PM returns to an in-progress step mid-way, what should happen?
answer: a + c. Resume where left off with answers preserved, and allow editing previous answers. PM can also inject new information/requirements mid-session — the AI should recognize new requirements and generate follow-up questions to cover them, not just continue the original question sequence.

question: What does switching to Review mode do?
answer: a) Shows the generated artifacts (milestones, requirements docs, etc.) read-only

question: What can the PM do with a generated artifact from inside the app?
answer: View, Download (as file), Copy to Clipboard

question: How does AI interaction work for artifact generation?
answer: AI generates complete artifact first. PM can then: (1) view it, (2) edit it inline directly, (3) prompt the AI to make specific changes to the document — collaborative editing with AI assistance post-generation.

question: When is a project done in Sherpy and what happens to it?
answer: c) PM manually marks it complete or archived

question: Authentication — who can access Sherpy projects?
answer: Current phase: MSW only, no real backend. Auth is mocked. Ultimate target: Okta SSO. This phase focuses on nailing application flow and developer experience before building the real backend. Auth model will be per-user accounts — each PM sees their own projects.

question: What does success look like at the end of this MSW phase?
answer: d) All of the above — full happy path demo-able to stakeholders. Exception: ONE real endpoint even in MSW phase — a single API endpoint that proxies to AWS Bedrock for AI integration. All other data/auth is mocked via MSW.
